notes:
Summary: Copperpine is a mid-stage contact center platform serving financial products (mortgages, loans, wealth). They want real-time agent-assist: streaming suggestions that appear to agents as they type/receive utterances, plus automated tool-calls (balance lookup, account freeze) and short ticket summarization after calls. Key ask: robust low-latency SLOs and predictable behavior during spikes.

Key stakeholders: Ellen Park (Head of CX) — primary buyer; Gregorio Silva (CTO) — infra/security approval; Linda Morris (Dir. Ops) — acceptance criteria owner.

Latency/throughput targets (customer-specified): p95 suggestion latency <= 150ms end-to-end for 1:1 agent sessions under normal load; sustained support for 600 concurrent agents with burst to 2k for seasonal spikes; goal: mean time-to-suggestion < 80ms in optimized runs.

POC acceptance criteria (agreed): 1) p95 suggestion latency < 150ms under simulated 2x baseline load, 2) suggestion relevance >= 90% on provided eval set, 3) successful function/tool-calling flows for 5 exemplar actions (balance_lookup, auth_check, account_freeze, escalate_ticket, case_link), 4) security sign-off: SOC2+KMS + no data retention beyond 30 days for ephemeral caches, 5) model fallback works with degraded UX but no errors.

Security/compliance notes: must support VPC/private deployment; data residency: US-East for PII; retention controls: configurable, default 30d for live session artifacts; strict redaction pipeline for PII in transcripts; legal insists on "no training on customer data" contractual clause. They requested pen-test timeline and SOC2 report copy (open).

Integration notes: primary contact center is Genesys Cloud (real-time events via websockets) with Zendesk ticketing for post-call summaries. Need session affinity + sticky KV cache for hot contexts, and token reuse across rapid successive requests. Recommended flow: continuous streaming RPC for suggestions, optimistic prefix caching + model route fallback to quantized variant when GPU capacity constrained.

Cost sensitivity: enterprise budget but concerned about per-token costs at scale. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching windows, quantization profile) and reserved dedicated pools for predictable unit economics.

Quotable from call: "We need suggestions that feel instantaneous — agents can't wait. If latency slips during holidays, our CSAT drops and turnover spikes." — Ellen Park.

Open items: detailed network egress diagram from their infra team, final GPU instance type for on-prem appliance, SLA language for failover to hosted fallback.

Next tactical steps: deliver POC plan + test harness by 2026-03-12; schedule load run (2x baseline) 2026-03-20; share SOC2/pen-test artifacts; finalize procurement template.
